answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each agent identity to present a fresh enclave quote, verifiable against the platform attestation chain and bound to its MRENCLAVE code measurement. A copied VM can duplicate software state but cannot forge a quote from genuine hardware; under a one-agent-per-attested-platform policy, creating more identities therefore requires acquiring physical silicon, not merely cloning virtual machines. The knoll, opal, and dawn labels add no trust: verification rests on the cryptographic evidence.
